title: Shared-module architecture guardrails and CI enforcement
problemStatement: The H30/H31/H32 review program produced a durable shared-module census and consumer map, but nothing in CI was turning that inventory into enforceable architecture rules. That left the repo vulnerable to new ownership drift, stale consumer-map artifacts, and fresh runtime dependencies on tools/shared that would quietly bypass the review findings.

duplicateClusters.name: Shared-module policy checks spread across partial validators
duplicateClusters.bestFix: Add one boundary guard that consumes the same generated ledger and enforces exact ownership, consumer-map consistency, and a waiver-backed src/** -> tools/shared/** boundary rule.

whyCurrentSharedModulesWereInsufficient: The generated ledger already knew ownership and consumer edges, but existing tests only validated artifact presence and basic gap counts.
There was no machine-readable waiver surface for currently-known runtime dependencies on tools/shared.

migrationsCompleted.notes: Now enforces ownership uniqueness, consumer-map consistency, and the waiver-backed src/** -> tools/shared/** boundary rule.
Records the currently-approved boundary exceptions and fails on stale or missing waivers.

nonGoals: Automatically migrating the waived runtime imports in the same change.
Creating a generic import-linting framework for every architectural boundary in the repository.
Blocking all src/** -> tools/** imports regardless of current ownership evidence.
followOnDeletionTargets: Remove waiver entries as H31/H32 adoption work migrates the remaining runtime consumers away from tools/shared.
Tighten the boundary guard further once the waived edges are eliminated.
